correctness.rationale: For all n>=4, the complement-of-disconnected-triples dual is characterized as sets with induced nonedge degree at most one. Cubicity and odd-order matching parity bound its faces at four vertices; triangle-freeness makes its tetrahedra precisely n squares. The 2n straight-rim triangles and four triangle faces per square are removed by 2n+4n explicitly proved free pairs. Their shared rungs are never removed, and the residual connected graph has 2n(n-3) edges and 2n vertices. Integral Alexander duality gives reduced Z-homology only in degree 2n-4 with rank 2n(n-4)+1. The cut complex contains the full (2n-6)-skeleton, so Hurewicz and Whitehead upgrade to the exact integral homotopy equivalence. Direct all-subset facet comparisons for n=4..7, complete collapse checks n=4..13 and independent mod-two chain ranks n=4,5,6 passed; finite checks are not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The same graph and ordinary 3-cut parameter are explicitly not settled in Agarwal--Basak (arXiv:2608.30601, Problem 19). The original ordinary-cut paper arXiv:2304.13675 and its 2024 sequel do not classify Möbius ladders. Public indexed records concern the total Möbius-ladder 3-cut complex (different faces), the ordinary circular ladder 3-cut complex (different graph, opposite bipartiteness), or graph classes with no or edge-disjoint squares (excluded by shared rungs). Searches did not identify a stronger implication. The indexed record summaries were compared at claim level, but absence from an index does not prove novelty.
residual_risks: An uncatalogued theorem about twist-invariant cut complexes or cubic square strips could imply the statement.
Three closely related indexed records were compared by exact claim summary, not their inaccessible complete full texts.
Finite verification has a bounded n range, but the proof of uniform free faces is symbolic for all n>=4.

value.rationale: The Möbius ladder is a canonical vertex-transitive cubic family and its cut-complex homotopy was explicitly raised in the primary 2026 literature (Problem 19). A new uniform integral homotopy classification for all n>=4 resolves a natural k=3 part of this direction, with exact sphere multiplicities and an explicit topological collapse explaining them. It also establishes the surprising equality of stable sphere counts for twisted and untwisted ladder graphs despite opposite bipartiteness. This is a complete motivated infinite-family classification, not arbitrary numerical sampling or a renamed known object.
